design_summary.pipeline: deterministic tokenize -> explode blocks into classifiable units -> optional LLM relabeling (batched) -> reassemble blocks using ORIGINAL text + new labels -> render Markdown -> validate -> save
design_summary.safety_property: The LLM is given only numbered text previews and returns ONLY {index, label} pairs -- it never outputs document text. Our code always splices the original, untouched block text back in. This makes content mutation structurally impossible (not just detected after the fact); validation is mostly schema-level (JSON parses, one label per index, no duplicates/out-of-range, label in allowed enum) rather than fuzzy text-diffing.
design_summary.batching: Units packed greedily into batches sized to fit num_ctx (~4 chars/token estimate, 900-token reserved overhead, max 18 units/batch). Batches run sequentially, carrying a 'heading stack' (last seen heading_1/2/3 titles) forward as context for the next batch.
design_summary.fallback_granularity: Per-batch: if one batch's response is malformed/incomplete, only that batch's units revert to their deterministic labels -- not the whole document.
design_summary.trigger_rule: Runs only if ENABLE_LLM_NORMALIZATION=true AND (force_llm_normalization=true OR structure_confidence is low/medium). Never runs automatically on structure_confidence=high documents. Skips (does not run) if the estimated batch count exceeds LLM_NORMALIZATION_MAX_BATCHES, unless force=true.

new_issues_observed_not_present_in_deter: The document's subtitle line (correctly a plain paragraph in the deterministic pass) was wrongly promoted to a second level-1 '#' title heading.

The 7 structurally-identical mini-framework labels (Cue/Action/Proof/Feedback/Identity/Value/Next Path) were classified inconsistently: 4 as bullets, 2 as heading_2, 1 as plain paragraph -- same semantic role, three different treatments.
Heading level drift across batch boundaries: sections 4/5 landed at heading_3 instead of heading_2, despite the heading-stack context-carrying mechanism.

honest_assessment: The safety design is fully validated: across 145 classified units and 9 real LLM batches, content preservation was perfect (identical word multiset, order, and char count) -- the label-only architecture worked exactly as designed, with zero content mutation even though the model's labeling was imperfect. On label QUALITY specifically: the two originally-reported issues (flow-line-as-heading, list-intro-as-bullet for QR/GPS check-in) are reliably fixed. However, the LLM pass also introduced new structural inconsistencies not present in the deterministic-only output (duplicate title heading, heading-level drift between batches, inconsistent treatment of repeated framework labels). Net structural quality is a mixed improvement, not a clean win, on this one real document. This matches the predicted risk in the Step 2.5 plan ('a wrong label is still possible; this is a quality risk, not a corruption risk') and is exactly why ENABLE_LLM_NORMALIZATION defaults to off and this is being reported for your review rather than enabled automatically.
